wholeFormReview.contentRead: Entire actual task, full reference solution, all four scoring steps, coverage metadata, five direct prerequisite contracts and all 58 normalized support goal descriptions and relations.
wholeFormReview.judgement: The call-centre data form a coherent data-model-simulation problem. The explicit Bernoulli assumptions distinguish the binomial model from its Poisson approximation; the table comparison and simulation discussion appropriately limit the conclusions about independence and time-constant rate. All numerical values were independently recomputed. The ordinary 20-point maximum and 10-point pass are retained. No formal derivation is scored.
wholeFormReview.sourceJudgement: BY M12.2 supports random variables, parameter interpretation and binomial contextual modelling. The BY additional statistics module supports data criticism and statistical methods but does not name Poisson or require its formal limit. SH pages 70-73 support distribution modelling, expected frequency interpretation and software simulation, and name binomial/hypergeometric and normal methods rather than this Poisson limit. Therefore the complete Poisson exercise is accepted as additional own SkillPilot content in the already theory-inclusive selected LK targets, with no new claim of official compulsory coverage. The new BY wrapper identifies additional SkillPilot work. SH reuses the existing collection path; approval relies on the explicit published source/scope decision and does not falsely claim that a new visible SH wrapper was materialized.

nineDirectPreparationDecisions.reason: The observed-versus-expected frequency comparison and the distinction between model compatibility and proof are central to part 2. Prior histogram and descriptive-measure work supports this judgement; this item does not separately assess every representation.

Having simulated experiments and inspected frequency variation is sound preparation for designing the simulation check in part 4. The written explanation is not a performance certificate for actually operating software; the coverage list correctly does not claim that.

Prior empirical location and dispersion work gives substance to the comparison of deviations and typical fluctuations. This is broader preparatory experience, not a claim that the examination calculates empirical mean and variance.

Part 1 now explicitly asks for the binomial model, rare-single-event approximation, lambda and probabilities; part 3 uses independent aggregation. This directly supports the existing nonempty assessed-content coverage. One time-interval model is an appropriate instance; an additional area-density variant is not required.

Accepted deliberately as theory-before-application preparation in these already theory-inclusive LK targets. Deriving the fixed-mean rare-event limit explains why many opportunities and small individual probability matter, why lambda=np is retained, and why the finite binomial model is only approximated. This is a coherent stronger teaching sequence, although formal derivation is not logically necessary for these computations. Approval does not depend on closing its graph endpoint and does not make this limit official BY/SH compulsory content. No formal proof is asked for, scored, covered or separately certified.
Part 3 explicitly requires V=Gh/3 and an interpretation against the corresponding prism. This is a direct preparatory and assessed-content relationship.

The reference method proves perpendicularity by AB dot AC=0 and fits a spatial-vector course. The general 4-point rubric accepts a correct right-angle proof, so this review does not assert that every successful response must calculate a dot product: the coordinate-axis argument is also mathematically sound. Keeping the reviewed vector-bearing preparation boundary and withholding scopes without this target is appropriate for reuse of this unchanged course task.

The solid-volume computation and cubic scaling require interpreting the shape and relating length, area and volume. The existing broad solid-volume goal is a suitable prerequisite and assessed-content reference; no mastery of all solid variants is inferred.
Part 2 uses the right-triangle properties to choose and evaluate the base-area formula. This directly supports the reference without requiring an exhaustive sample of every plane figure.
